airport.name: Glasgow Valley County Airport Wokal Field

summary: Glasgow Valley County Airport (Wokal Field) serves Glasgow, a small city in northeastern Montana situated along the Missouri River in the state's Hi-Line region. The airport provides critical air access for the surrounding agricultural and ranching communities of Valley County, connecting this remote area to larger Montana hubs. As a medium-sized regional facility, it supports both scheduled commercial service and general aviation operations.
faqs:
Q: What commercial service is available at Glasgow Valley County Airport?
A: The airport primarily offers regional scheduled service connecting Glasgow to larger Montana cities, with Cape Air historically providing flights to Billings and other regional destinations.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Glasgow?
A: The airport is conveniently located just a few miles from downtown Glasgow, making the drive typically under 10 minutes.

Q: Are there car rental services at the airport?
A: Yes, car rental agencies typically operate at the airport, though availability may be limited and reservations are recommended given the rural location.

Q: Does the airport have an FAA control tower?
A: Yes, the airport operates with a staffed control tower during operating hours and provides full general aviation services.
transport_tips: Renting a car is the most practical way to reach Glasgow and explore the surrounding region, as public transit options are extremely limited in this rural area. The airport is just a short drive east of the city center, with straightforward access via Highway 2. Many visitors arrange ground transportation in advance, as on-demand taxi service can be sparse in northeastern Montana.
local_tip: If you have time before or after your flight, visit the nearby Fort Peck Dam and its massive reservoir—one of the largest earth-fill dams in the world and a premier walleye fishing destination just a short drive south of Glasgow.
